Subject: Post-call: Air-gapped/private appliance – follow-ups & checklist

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we don’t lose momentum.

Recap (from our call)
- Preferred deployment: Private appliance, air-gapped (no outbound internet from cluster).
- Desired perf: 80–120 qps for internal inference workloads, expected peak concurrency 18–24 simultaneous sessions.
- Hardware preference: BioSynth leaning toward H100 (availability permitting) for training-like workloads; asked about minimum viable config.
- Procurement timeline: Marco indicated intent to start procurement in mid-March, target install late April.

Action items / clarifying questions (we need answers to the numbered items so our infra team can finalize BOM + SOW):
1) Rack & power: how many racks can you dedicate? per-rack power capacity (per-circuit amps & breaker type). 2U/3U constraints?
2) Shipping/receiving: any export/import rules, advance notice for shipments, or restricted carriers?
3) Maintenance window: preferred cadence for quarterly patching and emergency patching blackout windows?
4) KMS/HSM: do you have an on-prem HSM we should integrate with, or do you prefer Redwood-managed keywrap delivered via sealed media?
5) On-site ops team: name and contact for the systems admin who will coordinate racking, cabling and local network (we need a point-of-contact for the install runbook).

Attached: Redwood_Private_Airgap_Prereqs_v1.pdf (hardware/ops checklist) — this is our canonical prereq doc.

Next steps we propose
- Please review the attached prereqs and reply inline to the five clarifying items above (ideally by EOW 2/19).
- Schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive with Vivek (infra lead) to validate network & KMS flow (proposed slots: 2/22 9–11am PT or 2/23 1–4pm PT).
- Marco: if procurement has a template PO or required fields for SOW, please send. Laura will draft SOW once we have hardware footprint locked.

Thanks — I’ll coordinate the calendar after we hear back.

Ben — thanks for the thorough recap. I confirmed a few items with our facilities and infra team; answers below inline.

1) Rack & power: We can commit 2 full racks in our primary datacenter (Floor 3, Row B). Each rack has two 30A circuits (208V) and one 20A general purpose circuit. Rack u-space currently at 42U per rack, we can allocate up to 20U per appliance if needed.
2) Shipping/receiving: We have a security desk that must be notified 48 hours in advance. We prefer shipments via our contracted carrier (GlobalFreight) and cannot accept shipments from courier services flagged on our restricted-vendor list.
3) Maintenance window: Preferred maintenance windows are Sat 00:00–06:00 local (Pacific). Emergency change window limited — needs 24h advance notice unless it’s a critical security patch.
4) KMS/HSM: We have an on-prem HSM (nCipher) and would like to integrate; please send the KMS integration checklist. If integration is not possible for certain flows, we can consider sealed-key transfer.
5) On-site ops contact: Olivia Zhang (olivia.z@biosynth.com), Systems Ops Manager — she will be the primary on-site POC.

I attached the rack inventory we discussed (Biosynth_Site_Rack_Inventory.xlsx). Also: we do expect some areas to be physically air-gapped from our corporate network; need to understand how Redwood’s install images are validated offline.

Appreciate the quick answers and the inventory — that helps a lot. A few clarifications and what we’ll provide next:

- Hardware: based on your preference for H100 and the throughput target, our preliminary BOM is 2x H100 nodes (4x H100 if you want active/active for redundancy). Vivek will confirm final sizing after the deep-dive.
- Power & racking: 20U per appliance is fine; we’ll send exact U and inlet type once the node SKUs are finalized.
- Shipping: Redwood will coordinate with GlobalFreight and provide TWIC/export docs; we’ll need the 48h arrival notification.
- Maintenance & upgrades: We support an offline upgrade flow for air-gapped sites — signed image bundles + SHA256 checksums on USB (or encrypted disk) and a validation procedure. We keep a secure chain-of-trust: images are signed by Redwood’s release key; you can verify signatures locally.
- KMS/HSM: good news — we support nCipher via PKCS#11 for key wrapping and can run the key exchange with your HSM during install. Vivek will send a short KMS integration checklist (HSM model + firmware required fields).

Deliverables from Redwood this week:
- Airgap_Upgrade_MOP_v0_9.pdf (draft runbook for offline upgrades and image validation).
- A short KMS/HSM integration checklist (Vivek will post this separately).

Request: please confirm the deep-dive slot that works for your infra team (we proposed 2/22 9–11am PT or 2/23 1–4pm PT). If neither works, propose two alternatives and we’ll triage.

Claire / Olivia — quick technical notes ahead of the deep-dive. I’ve kept these high level; we’ll verify specifics during the session.

1) Image & upgrade validation (air-gapped flow)- We sign every image with an on-prem truststore key; bundle includes image, signature (.sig), and SHA256. Validation steps we recommend:
  - Verify signature with Redwood public key (we will provide a fingerprint and the public cert via a signed PDF).
  - Confirm SHA256 checksum matches the bundle.
  - Boot from external media in maintenance mode to apply the image (no inbound network required).

2) KMS/HSM integration- Supported: nCipher (PKCS#11). Requirements:
  - HSM reachable from management VLAN during initial key import (over air-gapped network).
  - Firmware >= 11.2 (please confirm your firmware version).
  - We support both keywrap and sealed-key exchange; for sealed-key we deliver wrapped keys on encrypted USB with an out-of-band passphrase exchange.

3) Spare parts & uptime recommendations- Recommend: 1 spare PSU per rack, 2 spare NVMe drives, 1 spare management NIC. For 99.9% SLA target, plan for N+1 GPU redundancy or cold-standby node.

4) Support model for emergency patches- We can provide: a) signed emergency patch bundle on encrypted USB within SLA window (requires shipping agreement), or b) provide a validated procedure and allow your team to run verification and apply patch locally (we will support via phone and pre-shared runbooks).

Prep for the deep-dive
- Please share nCipher model + firmware and the local systems admin contact (Olivia — can you confirm if you want the deep-dive to include your facilities team for rack/power Q&A?).

I’ll upload the KMS checklist and short runbook to the shared drive and Ben will link the doc. Looking forward to the session.
